Beaumont-Hamel British Cemetery is a Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery located in the Somme region of France. It is situated near the village of Beaumont-Hamel and is the final resting place for soldiers who fought and died during the First World War.

The cemetery contains the graves of over 700 Allied soldiers, primarily British and Commonwealth troops, who were killed during the Battle of the Somme in 1916. Many of the soldiers buried at Beaumont-Hamel died during the disastrous first day of the battle on July 1, 1916, when Allied forces suffered heavy casualties.

In addition to the graves of individual soldiers, the cemetery also features several memorials and monuments dedicated to different units and regiments that fought in the area. One of the most prominent features of the cemetery is the Beaumont-Hamel Newfoundland Memorial, which commemorates the soldiers of the Newfoundland Regiment who fought and died during the Battle of the Somme.

Visitors to Beaumont-Hamel British Cemetery can pay their respects to the fallen soldiers, learn about the history of the Battle of the Somme, and reflect on the sacrifices made by those who served in World War I. The cemetery is a poignant reminder of the devastating impact of war and serves as a place of remembrance for those who gave their lives in the conflict.
